claims.text: A nanoscale Ni-P or Al2O3 coating will increase the mechanical strength of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
A nanoscale Ni-P or Al2O3 coating will improve the fatigue resistance of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
Coated MnNiSi-based materials will largely retain the intrinsic large magnetocaloric effect of the uncoated material.
Ni-P and Al2O3 are examples of materials that can be used as nanoscale coatings for mechanical enhancement.
A nanoscale coating will act as a protective barrier against surface crack initiation.
A nanoscale coating will mitigate crack propagation from the surface and reinforce structural integrity.
Nanoscale coatings can exploit size-dependent effects to produce mechanical strengthening.
Size-dependent coating effects improve fatigue and deformation resistance by limiting the propagation of surface defects.
A sufficiently thin coating will minimally interfere with the magnetic domains responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Keeping the coating thin will leave the bulk microstructure governing magnetocaloric properties largely unaltered.
Preserving the bulk microstructure will preserve the magnetic entropy change.
Relative to uncoated MnNiSi-based material, coated samples will have higher tensile strength and longer fatigue life.
Relative to uncoated MnNiSi-based material, coated samples will exhibit a magnetic entropy change similar in magnitude to the baseline.
An excessively thick coating may reduce the magnetocaloric effect.
An incompatible coating material may alter the magnetic transition or operating-temperature range.
The mechanical enhancement and any magnetocaloric reduction will depend on coating material, thickness, and deposition parameters.
